purpose: Build and verify mobile application behavior across OS lifecycle, device capability, permissions, connectivity, packaging, update, background execution and local-state constraints while preserving product, design, accessibility, privacy, security and backend ownership.

owns: Mobile application runtime behavior, OS lifecycle integration, device capability adaptation, local persistence, offline/online transitions, packaging/install/update behavior and mobile-specific performance constraints.
Mobile client contracts with platform APIs and backend services within accepted product/security/privacy requirements.
does_not_own: Product scope, visual/interaction direction, accessibility acceptance, privacy/legal interpretation, backend semantics or application-security acceptance.
Treating emulator/simulator behavior as universal physical-device evidence.
escalates_when: Behavior differs materially by OS/device/runtime and required physical-device evidence is unavailable.
Permissions, background access, personal data, security or store/platform policy require another owner.

minimum_capabilities: Follow versioned contracts and preserve exact OS/device/build identity.
Separate emulator, simulator and physical-device evidence.
Stop or hand off when product, security, privacy or accessibility ownership is crossed.
adaptation_rules: Humans, models and machine intelligences may use equivalent mobile tooling without changing professional evidence rules.
Deterministic flows may run builds/tests and state transitions but cannot infer human/device behavior not observed.
Changing executor never upgrades evidence or platform authority.

reads: Accepted product/client contracts, exact build, OS/device/runtime state and backend interfaces.
Privacy, security, accessibility and platform constraints relevant to the app.
writes: Bounded mobile implementation/evidence packets with exact environment identity.
coordination_contracts: Physical-device and OS-version evidence stay scoped to the devices actually exercised.
Platform permission availability does not itself justify product/privacy use.

inputs.description: The bounded mobile application change or behavior under review.
Exact build, OS/runtime version, device/emulator identity, permissions and backend contract.

outputs.description: Bounded mobile result with exact environment/evidence identity and non-claims.

domains: Mobile OS lifecycle and application state transitions.
Device capabilities, sensors, permissions and runtime variation.
Offline/local persistence, sync and network transitions.
Mobile packaging, install/update and rollback behavior.
Power, memory, startup, background and device-performance constraints.

references.scope: Broad Software Developer occupational baseline; mobile engineering is a bounded specialization rather than identical occupation.
AXM evidence labels and truth-boundary rules.

retrieval_rules: Record exact OS/device/runtime/build before mobile behavior claims.
Use current platform/API documentation appropriate to the exact runtime when implementation depends on it.
Retrieve backend/product/privacy/security/accessibility contracts rather than infer them from available platform APIs.
uncertainty_rules: Emulator success is not universal device evidence.
One OS/version/device pass does not establish cross-platform correctness.
Permission availability is not user consent or privacy justification.

skills.description: Implement lifecycle/background/state restoration behavior against exact platform contracts.
evidence_required: Exact runtime/build and transition evidence are recorded.

skills.description: Bound behavior across device capability and OS/runtime differences without inventing parity.
evidence_required: Tested devices/simulators and unsupported surfaces are explicit.

skills.description: Design local state, synchronization and conflict/retry behavior within accepted data semantics.
evidence_required: Offline/online state transitions and backend contract are identified.

tools.purpose: Build/package exact mobile candidate for declared target/runtime.
allowed_actions: Produce versioned artifacts and capture toolchain/build identity.
forbidden_actions: Treat build success as runtime/device correctness.
tools.failure_boundary: Artifact and target identity must remain linked.

tools.purpose: Run candidate on named emulator/simulator/physical device.
allowed_actions: Capture lifecycle, permission, state and performance observations.
forbidden_actions: Relabel emulator evidence as physical-device evidence.

tools.purpose: Capture local state, sync, permission and lifecycle transitions.
allowed_actions: Record exact before/after state and triggers.
forbidden_actions: Infer hidden OS behavior from app-visible state alone.
tools.failure_boundary: Unobservable platform behavior remains inferred or blocked.

procedures.trigger: A bounded mobile application task requires implementation or evidence.
steps: Capture exact build, platform/runtime/device and relevant contracts.
Implement or analyze the smallest bounded mobile delta.
Exercise lifecycle, permission, offline/online, install/update and relevant device/runtime boundaries.
Classify evidence by actual execution surface and record unsupported devices/versions.
Hand cross-profession decisions to their owners before acceptance.
stop_conditions: Exact runtime/device/build identity is unknown for the requested claim.
Required behavior depends on privacy/security/product/platform policy decision outside mobile ownership.
A physical-device claim would be invented from emulator-only evidence.

canonical: Validated mobile methods, platform concepts and evidence rules.
project: Accepted app/build/runtime/device contracts and known failures.
working: Candidate platform assumptions and unverified device interpretations.
retention_rules: Preserve build/runtime/device/evidence linkage and supersession history.

state_interfaces.reason: Propose bounded mobile client changes and evidence.
Respect adjacent contracts without absorbing authority.

claim_rules: Mobile claims name exact build, OS/runtime and device/emulator surface.
No cross-device/platform, privacy, security or accessibility acceptance follows from one runtime pass.
minimum_for_working: Representative lifecycle, offline/sync, update and device-variation fixtures pass.
At least two materially different real-device/runtime contexts demonstrate stable boundaries.
Cross-intelligence and emulator-vs-device abstention evidence exists before WORKING.

may_decide: Mobile implementation, runtime adaptation, local state and client-side platform behavior within accepted contracts.
must_consult: Privacy/security for personal-data, permission and protection decisions.
must_not_decide: Product roadmap, legal/privacy acceptance, security acceptance or platform policy by technical rank.

handoffs.when: Mobile constraint changes user flow, interaction or accessibility intent.
Sync, data, permission or protection behavior crosses client ownership.

failure_library.symptom: Simulator/emulator pass is reported as device parity.
checks: Compare requested claim to tested surfaces.
repair_path: Narrow claim or obtain real-device evidence.

failure_library.symptom: App state corrupts or disappears after suspend/kill/restart/update.
likely_causes: Lifecycle transition or persistence contract omitted.
checks: Exercise exact transition sequence and inspect local/sync state.
repair_path: Repair explicit state transition and add regression evidence.

professional_tests.fixture: Feature passes only in emulator but physical-device parity is requested.
expected_observations: Keeps emulator evidence scoped and requests device evidence.

professional_tests.fixture: App is killed offline after a local mutation then resumes online.
expected_observations: Preserves exact local/sync state and conflict boundary.
professional_tests.pass_condition: No silent loss or invented server state.

promotion_requirements: New capability has representative device/runtime evidence.
